entry.title: Written Reply by Minister for Law Mr Edwin Tong SC on Improving Barrier-Free Accessibility on Kusu Island

link.title: Written Reply by Minister for Law Mr Edwin Tong SC on Improving Barrier-Free Accessibility on Kusu Island

entry.content:
4 November 2026 Posted in Parliamentary speeches and responses

Name and Constituency of Member of Parliament
Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Member of Parliament for Radin Mas SMC)

Question
To ask the Minister for Law whether the Singapore Land Authority will review and improve barrier-free accessibility on Kusu Island, particularly access to the religious sites, to enable elderly devotees and persons with mobility difficulties to participate safely in the annual pilgrimage.

Written Answer by Minister Edwin Tong SC:

1.      Barrier free access is available on parts of Kusu Island, including a barrier-free walkway which connects the ferry landing point to the jetty and extends further into the island. During the annual Kusu pilgrimage, personnel are stationed along the walkway to assist visitors, and the Singapore Land Authority (SLA) puts up tents along the way to shelter them. These arrangements help elderly devotees and visitors with mobility difficulties move around the island safely and comfortably.

2.      The Chinese temple on Kusu Island is a short distance from the jetty, and has a ramp which provides access for wheelchair users.

3.      However, the natural terrain on Kusu Island constrains the provision of barrier-free access on parts of the island. It is currently not feasible to provide lift access to the shrines, which sits on higher ground and can only be reached by climbing about 150 steps. Handrails are provided along the steps for the safety of visitors.

4.      Within these site constraints, SLA will continue to do what it can and find practical ways to make visits safer and improve access, taking into account the island’s terrain and the space available at each site.

entry.title: Election of Ambassador Rena Lee to the International Court of Justice

link.title: Election of Ambassador Rena Lee to the International Court of Justice

entry.content:
3 November 2026 Posted in Press Releases

  1. The Government of Singapore congratulates Ambassador for International Law Rena Lee on her election as a Judge of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) for the 2027 – 2036 term. Ambassador Lee will begin her term as Judge of the ICJ in February 2027. Ambassador Lee is the first Singaporean and the first woman from Southeast Asia to be elected to the ICJ. This is a significant milestone for Singapore.  

  2. The ICJ is the United Nations’ (UN) principal judicial organ which settles legal disputes submitted by States in accordance with international law. It also gives advisory opinions on legal questions referred to it by authorised UN organs and specialised agencies. It comprises 15 judges from different UN Member States who are elected to nine-year terms. 

  3. On 3 November 2026, the UN held an election for five open seats on the ICJ for the 2027 – 2036 term. Voting was conducted in both the UN General Assembly (UNGA) and UN Security Council (UNSC) at the UN Headquarters in New York. Ambassador Lee secured an absolute majority in both the UNGA and UNSC, receiving 151 votes out of 191 votes in the UNGA and 13 votes out of 15 votes in the UNSC. The strong support reflects the international community’s strong trust and confidence in Ambassador Lee. The Government of Singapore wishes Ambassador Lee and the incoming ICJ bench a successful term.

  4. Minister for Foreign Affairs Dr Vivian Balakrishnan said: “My heartiest congratulations to Ambassador Lee on her well-deserved election to the International Court of Justice. The results demonstrate the international community’s recognition of Ambassador Lee’s strong abilities, extensive experience, and standing in international law. Singapore also deeply appreciates the votes of confidence from our many friends around the world. We are honoured that a Singaporean is given an opportunity to serve on the ICJ for the very first time.  As the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, the Court is an indispensable institution that upholds and advances international law. The Government of Singapore has full confidence that Ambassador Lee will discharge her duties as a Judge of the ICJ with independence and distinction, and we look forward to her contributions to the work of the Court.” 

  5. Minister for Law and Second Minister for Home Affairs Mr Edwin Tong SC said: “I am delighted to congratulate Ambassador Rena Lee on her election to the ICJ. It was a hard-fought campaign, and the support shown by UN Member States in New York is a strong endorsement of the international community’s confidence in Ambassador Lee’s deep legal expertise and her proven track record in international law. Singapore has long been a staunch defender of an inclusive and rules-based international order. For international law to truly work, it must be anchored in institutions that are trusted, credible and effective. The ICJ is one such institution. For it to remain strong and effective in upholding international law, its bench must continue to comprise well-qualified Judges who serve with integrity. I am confident, without reservation, that Ambassador Lee will rise to the challenge and make a meaningful contribution to the Court.” 

  6. Ambassador Lee said: “I am deeply honoured by the trust and confidence that the international community has placed in me. I am grateful to the many countries that have supported my candidature. The International Court of Justice plays a vital role in the peaceful settlement of disputes and the upholding of international law, particularly at a time of growing global uncertainty. I look forward to serving on the Court with independence, impartiality and integrity, and to contributing to its important work in the years ahead.” 

 

MINISTRY OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS 

MINISTRY OF LAW 

3 NOVEMBER 2026 

Last updated on 3 November 2026

entry.title: Speech by Senior Parliamentary Secretary, Ministry of Law & Ministry of Social and Family Development, Mr Eric Chua at 10th International Mediation Summit

link.title: Speech by Senior Parliamentary Secretary, Ministry of Law & Ministry of Social and Family Development, Mr Eric Chua at 10th International Mediation Summit

entry.content:
4 November 2026 Posted in Speeches

中国贸促会 聂文慧副 会长,

最高人民法院 茅仲华 副院长,

中国法学会 王振江副会长,

司法部 人民参与和促进法治局 杜亚玲 局长,

湖南省人大常委会胡旭晟副主任, 

各位嘉宾、各位朋友：

大家早上好！

开场

1.                 首先，感谢中国贸促会和国际商事争端预防与解决组织的盛情邀请。

2.                 这是我第一次到长沙。对我来说，长沙是一个新的地方，但对新加坡律政部而言，长沙却是熟悉的老朋友。现任律政唐振辉部长与律政部前副常任秘书潘家煌先生曾两次访问长沙，出席贸促会的国际商事法律合作论坛。出发前，唐部长还跟我提起，长沙人民热情好客，对当时受到的款待记忆犹新。

3.                 今天，我也很高兴能够来到长沙，延续双方的交流与友谊。

长沙的经济与法律服务发展

4.                 近年来，长沙的产业发展令人瞩目。从工程机械、电动汽车、半导体等高端制造业，到人工智能等新兴科技，长沙不断创新，展现蓬勃活力。

5.                 与此同时，长沙也积极加强法治建设，为企业发展保驾护航。2025年，湖南长沙涉外法务集聚区正式成立，长沙国际仲裁院也在同年9月揭牌。同时，湖南律师事务所也积极拓展海外业务，多家律师事务所已经在非洲、中亚以及东南亚等地设立分支机构, “出海”律所数量位居中国中部地区首位。

6.                 这些发展让我感到，新加坡与长沙都重视法治，都希望为企业营造稳定、可预期的营商环境，也都致力于提供多元、高效的争议解决服务。

7.                 正所谓：“法治是最好的营商环境。” 企业要走得远，不仅需要市场和商机，更需要清晰的规则，以及公正、高效的争端解决机制。

8.                 新加坡拥有国际商事仲裁、调解及诉讼等全方位争议解决机制，让企业能够根据实际需要，选择最合适的方式解决纠纷。长沙也在不断完善相关法律服务体系。双方可以相互借鉴、优势互补。

调解：以和为贵，合作共赢

9.                 今天是国际调解高峰论坛，我想特别谈谈商事调解。

10.             《增广贤文》里说到: “忍一时风平浪静，退一步海阔天空。” 这不仅是中华传统文化千百年来沉淀的智慧，也是一代代华人秉持的处世哲学。

11.             调解让当事人跳出非赢即输的零和思维，在解决分歧时保留沟通与合作的空间，既节省时间和成本，也有助于维护商业关系。调解与仲裁、诉讼相辅相成，已经成为国际商事争议解决体系不可或缺的一环。

12.             《新加坡调解公约》为国际商事调解提供跨境执行框架，进一步增强企业使用调解的信心。新加坡也致力于与中国和国际伙伴一同合作，推动商事调解的发展和专业化。

合作展望

13.             令人欣喜的是，新加坡与长沙在争议解决领域，已经建立了良好的合作基础。早在2006年，长沙仲裁委员会就与新加坡国际仲裁中心签署合作备忘录。去年12月，长沙举办了新加坡国际仲裁中心仲裁机制与前沿实务研讨会。今年7月，长沙市律协率领25名湖南及长沙律师，赴新加坡参加国际仲裁培训。

14.             展望未来，我期待双方从三个方面深化合作。

一、   加强机构与人员交流，增进互信。

二、   携手支持中国企业“走出去”。

三、   共同培养争议解决及涉外法律人才。

15.             Now, please let me elaborate in English.

16.             First, strengthening institutional and people-to-people exchanges and building trust. We would like to encourage more exchanges between our dispute resolution institutions, law firms and legal professionals. These could include study visits, professional seminars, and opportunities for our lawyers to share practical experience and learn from one another in cross-border legal work and dispute resolution cases. After all, meaningful cooperation begins with mutual understanding and grows through trust.

17.             Second, working together to support Chinese businesses venturing overseas. As more enterprises from Hunan and Changsha venture into international markets, their need for cross-border legal services will continue to grow. Singapore serves as a gateway to ASEAN and the wider international market.

18.             We are also home to Southeast Asia’s largest cluster of legal services, with a comprehensive suite of international dispute resolution services.  Singapore law firms have developed decades of experience and extensive professional networks, together with a deep understanding of the legal and business environments across ASEAN.

19.             By combining our complementary strengths and expertise, our legal professionals can work together to support businesses in areas such as cross-border investment, regulatory compliance, intellectual property protection and dispute resolution. Together, we can help businesses navigate complex legal challenges and expand into ASEAN markets with greater confidence.

20.             Third, investing in dispute resolution and cross-border legal talent development. Developing skilled legal professionals is key to advancing dispute resolution and cross-border legal services.

21.             Since 2018, the Singapore International Mediation Centre (SIMC) has conducted 8 specialised mediator training workshops in China, with a total of 148 Chinese lawyers and mediators completing the training. In July this year, the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) conducted a training programme for 25 lawyers from Hunan and Changsha, setting a good example for collaboration in legal talent development.

22.             By investing in our people, we can deepen mutual understanding, strengthen professional ties and lay a solid foundation for enduring partnerships.

结语

23.             各位朋友，新加坡与长沙虽然相隔千里，但我们有共同的目标，也有深厚的合作基础。我相信，只要双方继续加强交流、携手同行，就能把彼此的优势转化为共同发展的机遇。

24.             最后，我想以一句唐代诗人李白的诗句与大家共勉：“长风破浪会有时，直挂云帆济沧海。”

25.             愿新加坡与长沙的友谊历久弥新，法律合作不断深化，共同开创互利共赢的新篇章！也祝本届国际调解高峰论坛圆满成功！

26.             谢谢大家！<p></p>
